abstract: We construct explicit no-three-in-line subsets of a modular hyperbola in every translated square of side $4p$, where $p>3$ is prime. Two empirical six-point sheet masks are coupled by a physical-parity coloring on signed multiplicative cosets. Deleting at most twelve residue fibres gives $6p-78$ points and leaves the central square of side $2p$ empty. For $p\equiv1\pmod{12}$ and a nonsquare level, the construction has exactly $6(p-1)$ points, attaining the known carrier upper bound. We then permit local orientation changes along the coset index cycles. Fixed boundary trims cost at most sixteen points per interface. For each fixed $B\ge1$, the resulting family has at least $(6-4/B)(p-1)$ points and $(p-1)/(8B)$ independent bits, each supported on at most $8B$ fibres. Compatibility with a prescribed central cap is exactly a Boolean formula of clause width at most two. Extending an existing arithmetic source theorem to four periods and nonsquare levels supplies a linear clean central target whose pair-lines miss the full carrier, uniformly over all ring orientations. Only high-height two-old/one-new clauses remain. Exact integer controls verify the generators, boundary trims and Boolean interface. These results give classical-density rings with quantified local freedom; they do not establish a compatible linear insertion, an asymptotic improvement over $3/2$, or an unbounded family above $1.8$.
